reason: Sunlight can lift ocean water through evaporation, beginning its journey through the water cycle.
expectation: The Sun will warm the ocean and produce water vapour or a cloud.

effect: Evaporation provides the first stage of the water cycle; the vapour now needs to form clouds or rain.
reaction: The detail that dissolved salts remain behind is useful.
reason: Air may cool or lift the evaporated water, as it helped produce rain in the previous chapter.
expectation: The water vapour will condense into clouds or lead toward rain.

effect: The vapour has condensed into clouds; the next useful step is likely to bring their water onto land.
reaction: The distinction between invisible vapour and visible droplets is useful.
reason: Clouds over the stone crust may bring rain onto land, as needed to start rivers.
expectation: Rain will fall on the land and begin collecting or flowing.

effect: Clouds combined with Water to produce Rainfall, so the next step is to direct it across the land.
reaction: The compatibility feedback resolved my incorrect guess efficiently.
reason: Rainfall on the stone crust could collect or flow toward the ocean.
expectation: Rainwater will gather or begin flowing over the land.

effect: Rainfall on the stone crust created rivers, which can carry sediment toward the ocean.
reaction: The link between downhill flow, erosion and deposition is useful.
reason: Rivers meeting the ocean can deposit sediment and build a delta.
expectation: Sediment carried by the rivers will form a delta where they meet the ocean.

effect: Rivers cannot combine directly with the ocean; Earth and Sun are available partners.
reaction: I was surprised that the river–ocean combination did not work directly.
reason: Earth may supply the sediment that rivers deposit to build a delta.
expectation: The rivers will carry and deposit earth, forming a delta or a step toward one.

alternatives.reason: Sunlight may help keep water travelling, but the delta goal suggests trying Earth first.

effect: Rivers and Earth produced sediment, providing the material needed to build a delta.
reaction: The erosion and transport step makes the delta's material source clearer.
reason: Sediment reaching the ocean can be deposited where a river slows.
expectation: The sediment will form a delta at the river mouth, or advance toward one.

alternatives.reason: The river may need to carry the sediment before it can be deposited.

effect: Sediment combined with Rivers to make the delta, completing that goal. Keeping water travelling remains.
reaction: The automatic correction made the river's role in depositing sediment clear.
reason: Rivers can combine with Sun, and solar energy may help return their water to the atmosphere.
expectation: Sunlight will help move river water back into the water cycle.

effect: Rivers and Sun completed the water cycle and the remaining goal, tying evaporation and precipitation to solar energy and gravity.
reaction: The summary usefully brought the individual processes together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the delta was most worthwhile: making sediment first and then returning it to the river showed how erosion, transport and deposition connect.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to combine rivers directly with the ocean was less worthwhile as progress, though the feedback revealed useful partners.

surprise.text: I expected rivers meeting the ocean to make a delta directly, but the game required sediment and a separate combination with rivers.

arbitrary.text: Combining clouds with Water to make rainfall felt somewhat arbitrary: I expected clouds over land to produce rain, although the result explained droplet growth.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the water-cycle and delta sequences made familiar processes easier to connect, despite a few unintuitive pairings.
